what: A 1px underline that is always drawn sweeps out to the right end on hover, and .2s later a new line is drawn in from the left (.6s, cubic-bezier(.32,.95,.6,1)). On release it goes the same direction: the current line exits right and .2s later a new one is drawn again from the left. The two strands overlap as they pass, a baton hand-off where the line never breaks.

options.--fx-dur: Duration of the reveal and the drawn line (per style), default .6s
options.--fx-lag: Delay before the new line is drawn (via style), default .2s
options.look: With ”sweep” it is a single strand — on every hover the line retracts to the right end (first half) and is drawn again from the left (second half). Here --fx-dur defaults to .5s, the curve is ease, and --fx-lag defaults to 0 (.3s to draw after the link blur). With ”slide” the same single strand as sweep slides out to the right (translate 100% + scaleX 0) as it retracts and is drawn again from the left — whole run linear over --fx-dur (default .7s), each half fixed at cubic-bezier(.6,.18,.17,.72) (the original’s underline-sweep).
options.--fx-sweep-ease: a curve for each half of the sweep type (via style), default ease — the slide type lives inside keyframes so it is fixed at cubic-bezier(.6,.18,.17,.72)

note: Lines are drawn on the element’s ::before and ::after — if the element uses those elsewhere, attach them to an inner span
